headline: Springer says his best is still to come
standfirst: The German reached his first televised quarter-final at the Grand Slam and spoke about confidence, a tough Ally Pally memory and a kit mishap.
body: Niko Springer says the best version of his game has not yet been seen, even after he reached the first televised quarter-final of his career at the Grand Slam of Darts.

Springer beat Rob Cross 10-8 in Wolverhampton after leading and then being pegged back. Speaking to the media afterwards, including Dartsnews, he admitted his year had not been strong overall but said recent weeks had brought more consistency, which mattered with the World Championship approaching.
He is also looking forward to the Players Championship Finals, which he missed last year through illness. "I'm very happy to have that opportunity this year," he said, according to Dartsnews.

Springer was asked about his first-round loss to Joe Comito at Alexandra Palace and said the defeat took three to four months to get over, with a mental coach helping. He now says he is past it and eager to return to the stage.

The conversation also produced an unlikely story. Springer said he arrived at last year's UK Open having packed two right shoes, could not find a replacement in a supermarket and ended up borrowing a pair from Pero Ljubic. He still played Cor Dekker in his opening match, and said he averaged around 114 or 115.
His kit routine has not changed much: the shoes are around ten years old, and he picked up a second-hand pair this year to go with two practice and playing pairs.
His run adds to a good autumn for German darts, following Martin Schindler's run to the European Championship final.
